treatment.logline: A modest Colombo tea seller measures his cramped workplace against a larger ambition, then returns to the work that could make it possible.

arc.beat: Hospitality gives way to private appraisal
arc.feeling: Warmth followed by awareness of constraint

arc.beat: Ambition becomes explicit and returns to labour

treatment.approach: Grounded Sri Lankan everyday drama: let practical care establish character before the intimate statement of ambition. The genre facet here is hopeful working life, not suspense. Begin with a roadside master that contains the morning rhythm, then progressively privilege Kasun. Seven essential clips total 32 seconds, including preparation split for reliable physical actions. No montage material from other scenes is imported.

treatment.geography: Kasun stays screen left behind the counter, initially facing screen right. The customer approaches from screen right and faces left. The road lies beyond the customer's side. The flask remains in Kasun's left hand. When he surveys the vehicle and finally resumes work he faces away into its cramped interior; his outward glance restores the screen-right eyeline.
treatment.key_image: Kasun in a close single, the flask still in his left hand and the narrow vehicle fittings behind him, making a large promise in a small space.
advice: Keep the transaction routine; the customer has no supplied dialogue and must receive no invented words.
Use traffic depth and indistinct pedestrian movement rather than sharply featured additional people.
Preserve the pause of appraisal without suggesting defeat.
Preparation uses short editorial ellipses between distinct tasks; never demand a whole hand routine in one generation.

editor_notes: Intended cut: approximately 28 seconds; the 32-second must bin includes in-take handles, not 32 seconds of required screen time. Preserve the complete 2.7-second L6 performance.

The roadside master establishes the street and geography; the preparation single isolates the flask fill. The arrival master completes the counter-cleaning phase as the customer approaches. The shared counter view carries the smile and cup pickup; the later master keeps departure and appraisal in order. The close single carries the outward glance and L6; the final medium returns to work.

The three preparation tasks are divided across consecutive clips to avoid an unreliable hand routine. The kettle and cleaning cloth are implied by the specified preparation. The prepared tea is already on the counter before pickup; there is no direct hand-to-hand contact.

Kasun was not initially placed by the packet: he begins standing behind the counter at screen left. The initially unplaced customer approaches from screen right. The flask remains in Kasun's left hand. The customer carries the tea out to screen right.

Match the arranged food, flask, cloth, prepared cup and hand positions at cuts. The cup is on the counter before pickup and in the customer's right hand after it; the customer is off-screen before Kasun surveys the fittings. Match the inward-to-outward eyeline into the close single, and the outward-to-inward eyeline into the final medium.

The customer's request has no supplied wording: play the approach and attention to the tea cup without inventing dialogue. Lay continuous Colombo street ambience and restrained effects in post over the silent picture sources.
Avoid a close hand-to-hand transfer, elaborate pouring-and-resetting routines, sharp identifiable crowds and unsupported invented speech. No mirrors or complex physical contact are required.
Speed ramps, freeze frames, digital punch-ins and split screens are post-only possibilities; these locked clean sources do not require them, and none is part of the intended cut.
The supplied romantic montage and later struggle directions are scoped elsewhere and are not staged here. Preserve natural light and grounded performances as directed.

editor_notes: Intended cut: approximately 28 seconds; the 32-second must bin includes in-take handles, not 32 seconds of required screen time. Preserve the complete 2.7-second L6 performance.

The roadside master establishes the street and geography; the preparation single isolates the flask fill. The arrival master completes the counter-cleaning phase as the customer approaches. The shared counter view carries the smile and cup pickup; the later master keeps departure and appraisal in order. The close single carries the outward glance and L6; the final medium returns to work.

The three preparation tasks are divided across consecutive clips to avoid an unreliable hand routine. The kettle and cleaning cloth are implied by the specified preparation. The prepared tea is already on the counter before pickup; there is no direct hand-to-hand contact.

Kasun was not initially placed by the packet: he begins standing behind the counter at screen left. The initially unplaced customer approaches from screen right. The flask remains in Kasun's left hand. The customer carries the tea out to screen right.

Match the arranged food, flask, cloth, prepared cup and hand positions at cuts. The cup is on the counter before pickup and in the customer's right hand after it; the customer is off-screen before Kasun surveys the fittings. Match the inward-to-outward eyeline into the close single, and the outward-to-inward eyeline into the final medium.

The customer's request has no supplied wording: play the approach and attention to the tea cup without inventing dialogue. Lay continuous Colombo street ambience and restrained effects in post over the silent picture sources.
Avoid a close hand-to-hand transfer, elaborate pouring-and-resetting routines, sharp identifiable crowds and unsupported invented speech. No mirrors or complex physical contact are required.
Speed ramps, freeze frames, digital punch-ins and split screens are post-only possibilities; these locked clean sources do not require them, and none is part of the intended cut.
The supplied romantic montage and later struggle directions are scoped elsewhere and are not staged here. Preserve natural light and grounded performances as directed.
